where_we_are: Challenges A and B are done and delivered (repository public, email to the panel sent). KeysBench (STORY-004, optional) ran live in October 2026: 198 attempts stand, 17.81 USD with voided attempts included, results in keysbench/results/2026-10/results.md. Finding: on these six tasks the models separate on cost, not on whether they can do the work (B: 5 of 7 contestants passed every attempt, cost per pass 51 times apart; A0: 3 of 4, 77 times). Five of six tasks are saturated. Configuration A (the CLI with Python) was run and voided: the restricted CLI denied most of the Python its rule allowed (56 denials in 13 attempts). Decided by the repository owner on 2026-10-11: A is not run this month. On 2026-10-12 the challenges were reviewed live with the panel. STORY-005 (reject a component with a critical OSV vulnerability) was built during that session: a pure rule in core/vulns.py with six cases (S5-01 to S5-06), and no network adapter yet. When the model API is down the scan now refuses cleanly (exit 2, names the component) and writes no decision for it, so a re-run decides it when the model answers; the ledger keeps the decisions already made and the failed run, and the report refuses to be written until every component has a decision. An answer that cannot be read still ends in Needs review. Before 2026-10-12 this crashed with a raw traceback (S2-13).
